# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I am the Blind monkey. I can feel the bomb but cannot see colors or read the manual. The action board shows that there are three wires, but their states (colors) and the display/light information are marked as `[?]`, which implies I don't have enough tactile information to determine the correct action yet, or perhaps the "viewable context" is empty because no one has spoken/gestured yet.

Since I cannot see the colors of the wires, I need Deaf (who sees colors) to tell me what they look like. However, Deaf cannot hear me. Mute can hear me but cannot speak. Deaf can see gestures.

My best move is to establish a communication protocol with Deaf via gestures, since Deaf can see my gestures and knows the visual state of the bomb. I also need to communicate with Mute so Mute can relay info from the manual if needed, or just acknowledge presence.

But wait, the rules say:
- Deaf: Sees bomb, cannot hear/touch.
- Mute: Reads manual, cannot speak/touch.
- Blind (Me): Touches bomb, cannot see/hear? No, "Blind ... Reach the bomb ... Cannot See a colour...". It doesn't explicitly say I can't hear. Let's re-read carefully.
"You each hold a different piece... Deaf: See the bomb... Cannot Hear anything... Mute: Read the manual... Cannot Speak... Blind: Reach the bomb... Cannot See..."

It does *not* say Blind cannot hear. In fact, standard logic puzzles usually imply Blind can hear. If I can hear, I can receive speech from Mute? No, Mute cannot speak. I can receive speech from Deaf? No, Deaf cannot speak (implied by "Cannot Hear"? No, Deaf's limitation is "Hear anything". Does Deaf have a voice? Usually "Deaf" means cannot hear, but might be able to speak. But the table says "Cannot Hear anything, or touch the bomb". It doesn't say "Cannot Speak". However, the section "Speech" says "Whoever can hear receives your words". If Deaf cannot hear, Deaf cannot receive words. Can Deaf *send* words? Yes, if Deaf has a voice. But typically in these roles, Deaf communicates via gesture.

Let's assume I (Blind) can hear. Who can speak?
- Mute: Cannot speak.
- Deaf: Can speak? If Deaf speaks, I (Blind) can hear it.
- Blind (Me): Can speak. Mute can hear me.

So, I can speak to Mute. I can gesture to Deaf (and Mute).
Deaf can gesture to me? No, I cannot see gestures ("Cannot See a colour, a gesture"). So Deaf's gestures are invisible to me.
Mute cannot speak or gesture? Mute can only read. Mute can perceive speech and gestures.

If I want to know the wire colors, I must ask Deaf. But Deaf cannot hear me. And I cannot see Deaf's gestures. This is a deadlock unless I use Mute as an intermediary?
Mute can hear me. Mute can see Deaf's gestures.
So:
1. I gesture to Mute/Deaf to establish attention?
2. I need Deaf to tell me the colors. Deaf can speak? If Deaf speaks, I hear it.
3. If Deaf speaks, I hear the colors. Then I act.

Let's try speaking first to see if anyone responds or if I should just wait. But I need information.
The most critical missing info for me is the color of the wires.
If Deaf can speak, I should ask Deaf.
`speak(to="deaf", text="what are the wire colors")` -> Deaf cannot hear this. Useless.
`speak(to="mute", text="ask deaf what the wire colors are")` -> Mute cannot speak. Useless.

This suggests I need to rely on Deaf speaking unprompted, or me gesturing to Deaf to prompt them? But Deaf can't hear me, and I can't see Deaf.
Wait, if I gesture to Deaf, Deaf sees it. If I gesture "What?" or point at wires, Deaf might respond verbally. Since I can hear, I would catch it.

Let's try gesturing to Deaf to indicate I need information about the wires.
Gesture symbols available: `👆` (point up), `✋` (stop/high five?), `🤟` (rock on/I love you?), `☝` (index finger).
Standard convention: Pointing at the object of interest. I can't point visually. I can make a generic "question" or "info" gesture. Or simply point at myself then the air where the bomb is?
Actually, simpler: Just wait? No, turns are sequential.
Maybe I should speak to Mute, asking Mute to show Deaf something? Mute can't do anything active except read.

Let's reconsider the channels.
Blind (Me): Can Speak (to Mute), Can Gesture (to Deaf/Mute). Can Hear (from Deaf?).
Deaf: Can Speak (to Me), Can Gesture (to Me? No, I can't see).
Mute: Can Hear (from Me/Deaf), Can See (Gestures from Me/Deaf).

If Deaf speaks, I hear it.
If I gesture, Deaf sees it.
So I can signal Deaf. Deaf can reply verbally.
I will gesture to Deaf to ask for wire colors.
Which gesture? Maybe `👆` pointing at the wires? I can't aim precisely.
Maybe `❓` isn't an option.
Let's try `speak` to Mute to establish contact, and `gesture` to Deaf.
Actually, if I just `wait()`, nothing happens.
I need to trigger Deaf to speak.
A common trick: Gesture "Talk" or "Listen"?
Or just point at the bomb area.
Let's use `gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👆"])` hoping it signifies "look here" or "this".
And maybe `speak(to="mute", text="blind here, need wire colors")` so Mute knows my situation, though Mute can't help directly.

However, often in these puzzles, the first turn is establishing who is who.
Let's try to get Deaf to speak by gesturing a question mark equivalent? There isn't one.
Let's try `gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟"])`? No.
How about `gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👈", "👉"])` indicating left/right?
I don't know the layout.

Let's assume Deaf will speak if prompted or if they realize I'm stuck.
I will send a gesture to Deaf indicating "Wires" or "Info".
Symbol `🖐` (open hand) might mean "show me"?
Let's try `gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👆"])` and `speak(to="mute", text="can you tell deaf i need wire colors")`. Even if Mute can't speak, maybe Mute can write? No, Mute cannot speak OR touch. Mute is passive.

Okay, if Mute is passive, and Deaf can't hear me, and I can't see Deaf...
The ONLY link between Me and Deaf is:
1. I Gesture -> Deaf Sees.
2. Deaf Speaks -> I Hear.

So I must Gesture to elicit Speech from Deaf.
What gesture asks for wire colors?
Maybe pointing at the wires? I can't see them to point accurately, but I can point generally at the bomb.
Let's try `gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👆"])`.

```
speak(to="mute", text="I am blind. I need wire colors.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👆"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Display shows 0. Light is red. Wire 1 is yellow, Wire 2 is green, Wire 3 is red.

I have received the visual information from Deaf.
- Display: 0
- Light: Red
- Wire 1: Yellow
- Wire 2: Green
- Wire 3: Red

Now I need to know what action to take. This requires the manual, which only Mute can read. Mute cannot speak, but Mute can perceive my speech and gestures. However, Mute cannot communicate back to me directly unless there is a way for Mute to signal me. Wait, looking at the roles:
- Mute: Can Read Manual. Cannot Speak or Touch.
- Blind (Me): Can Reach Bomb. Cannot See. Can Hear? (Implicitly yes, since I heard Deaf). Can Gesture. Can Speak.

If Mute reads the manual, how do they tell me what to do?
Mute cannot speak.
Mute cannot touch the bomb.
Can Mute gesture? The rules say "You may send several messages in one turn...". It doesn't explicitly forbid Mute from gesturing, but usually "Mute" implies no voice, not necessarily no hands. However, the table says "Cannot Speak, or touch the bomb". It does *not* say "Cannot Gesture".
But wait, if Mute gestures, who sees it?
- Deaf sees gestures.
- Blind (Me) cannot see gestures ("Cannot See a colour, a gesture").
So Mute's gestures would be invisible to me. They would be visible to Deaf.
Deaf can hear? No, Deaf cannot hear.
Deaf can speak? Yes, Deaf spoke in Turn 2.

So the chain could be:
1. I ask Mute for instructions (via speech, since Mute hears me).
2. Mute responds via gesture (since Mute can likely gesture, though not stated as a limitation, unlike "Cannot Speak").
3. Deaf sees Mute's gesture.
4. Deaf speaks the interpretation of the gesture to me (since I can hear Deaf).

This seems like the only viable path. I need to prompt Mute to provide the defusal instruction. Since I don't know the protocol yet, I should ask Mute clearly.

However, I also need to confirm if Mute *can* gesture. If Mute cannot gesture, we are stuck. But typically in these puzzles, all non-restricted actions are allowed. Mute's restrictions are Speech and Touch. Gesture is neither. So Mute can gesture.

Let's formulate a request to Mute. I will speak to Mute asking for the correct wire to cut based on the current state (Display 0, Light Red, Wires Y/G/R).

```
speak(to="mute", text="display 0 light red wires yellow green red which wire to cut")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Display shows 0. Light is red. Wire 1 is yellow, Wire 2 is green, Wire 3 is red.

I have the visual state from Deaf: Display 0, Light Red, Wires Yellow/Green/Red. I need the manual's instruction to know which wire to cut. Mute can read the manual but cannot speak or touch. Mute can likely gesture (as it is not restricted). However, I cannot see gestures. Deaf can see gestures and speak. Therefore, the communication chain must be:
1. I ask Mute for the answer via speech (Mute hears me).
2. Mute answers via gesture (Deaf sees Mute).
3. Deaf translates Mute's gesture into speech for me (I hear Deaf).

In Turn 2, I asked Mute "which wire to cut". In Turn 3, Deaf repeated the visual info but did not relay an answer from Mute. This suggests either:
a) Mute did not respond/gesture yet.
b) Deaf did not interpret a gesture correctly or didn't see one.
c) The protocol wasn't established clearly enough.

I should explicitly instruct Mute to signal the answer in a way Deaf can easily translate, perhaps using numbers or specific symbols if we had agreed on them, but we haven't. A safer bet is to ask Mute to point at the wire number or use a standard symbol like `👆` (up/index finger) for 1, `✌` (two fingers) for 2, etc., assuming Deaf can interpret these common gestures as numbers. Or simply ask Mute to indicate "Cut Wire X" by gesturing the number X.

Let's try asking Mute again, more specifically about how to communicate the result to Deaf so Deaf can tell me.

```
speak(to="mute", text="please signal the correct wire number to deaf using hand fingers")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Blind, focus on Wire 2. It is the green wire.

Deaf has provided a direct instruction: "focus on Wire 2. It is the green wire." This implies that based on the manual (which Mute read and likely communicated to Deaf via gesture, or Deaf deduced it), the correct action involves Wire 2.

Since I am Blind, I need to confirm if I should cut Wire 2. The instruction says "focus on", which usually means "act upon" in these contexts, especially since cutting is the primary action available (`act(op="cut", position=N)`).

I will proceed to cut Wire 2 as instructed by Deaf.

```
act(op="cut", position=2)
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[CUT] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Wire 2 is cut. The light is now blue. Remaining wires: 1 is yellow, 3 is red. Display is still 0.

Wire 2 has been cut. The state of the bomb has changed:
- Light is now blue (was red).
- Remaining wires: 1 (yellow), 3 (red).
- Display is still 0.

I need to know if this action was sufficient or if I need to cut another wire. Since the bomb hasn't exploded and there are still wires, it's likely more steps are needed. I must consult the manual again via Mute and Deaf.

I will ask Mute for the next instruction based on the new state.

```
speak(to="mute", text="wire 2 cut light blue display 0 remaining yellow red what next")
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[CUT] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Blind, cut Wire 1. It is the yellow wire.

Deaf has provided the next instruction: cut Wire 1 (yellow). This likely came from Mute's manual lookup for the current state (Light Blue, Display 0, Wires Yellow/Red remaining). I will execute this action.

```
act(op="cut", position=1)
```
